name: Kate Bush
hook: A teenage songwriter whose demo David Gilmour paid for, who took up the Fairlight sampler in 1980, and who produced her own records from 1982.

blurb.age13: Kate Bush was born in 1958 in Bexleyheath, near London, and grew up in an old farmhouse in East Wickham. She was writing songs as a young teenager. When she was 16, David Gilmour of Pink Floyd paid for her to record a proper demo, and it got her a contract with EMI. In 1978, aged 19, her song 'Wuthering Heights' went to number one in Britain. She was the first woman to reach number one there with a song she wrote entirely herself. In 1980 she started using the Fairlight, an early sampler that could play back any recorded sound from a keyboard, and from 1982 she produced her own albums. In 2022 her 1985 song 'Running Up That Hill' was used in 'Stranger Things' and became a hit all over again.
blurb.adult: Born in Bexleyheath on 30 July 1958 and raised in East Wickham. David Gilmour financed a professional demo when she was 16, which led to her EMI contract. 'Wuthering Heights' (1978) made her the first female artist to reach UK number one with a wholly self-written song. She met the Fairlight CMI while singing backing vocals on Peter Gabriel's third album in early 1980 and used it prominently on 'Never for Ever' that year. 'The Dreaming' (1982) was the first album she produced herself, and every album since has been her own production; 'Hounds of Love' (1985) reached number one in the UK. She stopped touring after 1979 and did not play live again until a residency in 2014. 'Running Up That Hill' reached UK number one and US number three in 2022 after its use in 'Stranger Things'.

signatureTracks.title: Wuthering Heights
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Written as a teenager after a television adaptation of the novel: her first single and a UK number one.

signatureTracks.title: Babooshka
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Never for Ever', the first of her albums built with the Fairlight sampler; listen for the smashing glass.

signatureTracks.title: Running Up That Hill (A Deal with God)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Self-produced, built on a Fairlight and a drum machine, and a hit twice, 37 years apart.
